response:
It makes sense that you're struggling—those feelings didn't come from nowhere. You built genuine closeness over three years, then crossed into physical intimacy, and now you're being asked to file all of that under "friendship" while the flirtation and touching continue. That mixed signal keeps the hope alive, which makes moving on nearly impossible.

Here's the hard truth: you can't get someone out of your system while you're still receiving the exact input that feeds the fantasy. The constant physical contact and one-on-one talks keep reopening the wound. If you genuinely want to heal, you may need real distance for a while—fewer chats, gentle boundaries around the hugging, less reading into the glances. That might mean the friendship cools, at least temporarily, and it's worth asking yourself honestly whether a friendship on his terms is actually serving you.

You deserve someone who chooses you fully, not someone who keeps you close but just out of reach. Protecting your own heart isn't unkind—it's necessary.
